A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite substantial appendix reorganization.

before.justification: V1 reports original RNN training experiments, manifold reconstructions, runtime measurements, dynamical-system simulations and analysis of cortical-neuron recordings.

after.justification: V3 retains original experiments and adds quantitative manifold assessments, further runtime measurements and a human ECG reconstruction and chaos analysis.

M1.justification: The architectures, inverse-map heuristic, determinant regularizer and fallback algorithm remain. Algorithm 1 now constructs neighboring segments directly through PCA/kernel-PCA, whereas v1 preferred matching regional eigenspaces and used PCA conditionally. Appendix D adds an alternative graph/Taylor construction for distance calculations. The newly specified sampling distributions and kernel mainly expand implementation documentation.

E1.justification: V3 adds a human ECG reconstruction and chaos-detection example in Figure 10, extending empirical coverage beyond cortical-neuron recordings. The original main synthetic benchmarks remain, while appendix coverage of quasi-periodic and coexisting chaotic/periodic attractors is reduced.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain analytical and grid-based checks for the toy maps, numerical Lorenz manifold reconstruction, and regularization-on/off controls. The recursive homoclinic-checking algorithm is relocated, not newly introduced. Newly discussed SLDS, threshold-linear and control-system models are not evaluated as additional comparators.

E3.justification: V3 introduces a quantitative manifold-validation protocol using normalized closest approach to a saddle and on-manifold versus random-point controls; Figure 6A specifies 1000 points per group. New protocols include ECG evaluation with an 80-dimensional ALRNN and five-dimensional embedding, and Lorenz runtime testing at M=100. The existing training-table configurations remain numerically unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 4 and Appendix G add quantitative validation of previously illustrated manifolds. Runtime analysis expands from Duffing to Lorenz, and the ECG case adds perturbation-divergence, Lyapunov and homoclinic diagnostics. Conversely, v1's extensive parameter-dependent bifurcation, multistability and basin analyses in Figures 9–15 are removed. The original invertibility-regularization ablation remains.

E5.justification: V3 specifies three runs for the new Lorenz runtime experiment and reports ECG Lyapunov estimates across five initial conditions as mean ± SD. Table 2 also introduces median ± spreads without defining those spreads. These additions do not establish increased replication of existing experiments; their original run counts and significance tests remain.

E6.justification: V3 adds manifold-quality scores of 0.97, 0.95, 0.78 and 0.76 for Duffing, decision making, Lorenz and cortical recordings, respectively. It also reports basin-boundary distances, additional runtime results and an ECG maximum Lyapunov exponent of 0.0074 ± 0.00083. V1-only bifurcation and coexistence results disappear. These are added or removed outcomes, not demonstrated improvements in matched reconstruction performance.

T1.justification: V3 adds graph parameterizations, invariance equations and a Taylor construction in Appendix D, alongside the new manifold-quality definition. It corrects the stated discrete-time stability criterion from eigenvalue real-part signs to magnitudes relative to one. Explicit 2D inverse-map case analysis and cycle stability-region derivations are removed. The Jordan-block, homoclinic and matrix-power derivations are largely retained after relocation.

C1.justification: The abstract is unchanged. The introduction and conclusion retain the central contribution: a semi-analytical algorithm for stable/unstable manifolds in ReLU RNNs, enabling basin delineation and homoclinic-chaos detection. Additional diagnostics and the ECG example extend supporting demonstrations without redefining these central claims.

C2.justification: V3 interprets basin distances as approximately balanced choices and differential perturbation sensitivity in the neuron example. It adds qualifications concerning numerical drift, missed saddle points and extensions to SLDS and threshold-linear networks. The principal interpretations of multistability and chaos, and the existing fractal-geometry and scaling limitations, remain.

D1.justification: V3 documents QR-based sampling, Gaussian-mixture scales, the RBF kernel, training-loss details, benchmark parameters, histogram binning and runtime support-point budgets. However, v1 Appendix H.1's explicit trajectory-pool sampling and transient-removal instructions disappear. Appendix A adds a publication-time code promise rather than a usable access location. These changes concern documentation and do not establish reruns.

R1.justification: The introduction and conclusion substantially broaden positioning through engineering/control applications, threshold-linear networks, SLDS and Lur'e systems. New comparisons discuss continuity, time domain and weight restrictions. Meanwhile, the earlier robust-chaos literature discussion and several associated references are removed. This changes research positioning beyond bibliographic editing.

P1.justification: Section 3.3 is extensively rewritten into a numbered construction procedure with revised pseudocode and notation. The appendices are reorganized around derivation, construction, training, assessment, benchmarks and additional results, replacing the earlier map/chaos/multistability organization. Introduction and conclusion passages expand, and the acknowledgements section is removed.

P2.justification: V3 removes the earlier appendix figure suite and inverse-case tables, adds a manifold-quality table and multipanel figure, and introduces ECG and curvature figures. The runtime figure gains a Lorenz panel and revised horizontal-axis labeling. Figure 2 rearranges panels, while several retained figures and algorithms relocate. Some removed displays duplicate results still shown in Figure 5.

improvement.justification: V3 makes the method easier to assess through quantitative manifold diagnostics, clearer construction instructions and concrete implementation settings. Additional ECG and runtime checks broaden support. These benefits are partly offset by removing explicit 2D inverse derivations and regularization-sampling instructions, while some new uncertainty summaries remain undefined. The net improvement is supported but limited; general accuracy and scalability are still not comprehensively established.
